Subject: Redwood follow-up + security questionnaires

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo this morning - that throughput baseline looked promising for our use case. As we discussed, the security and compliance team wants to kick off the standard vendor security intake so we can move to security review. Can you share Redwood's SIG/CAIQ responses and any up-to-date SOC 2 artifacts or timeline for SOC 2 Type II? Also: a quick call with your security engineer would be helpful for a couple of clarifying items around PHI handling and data residency.

Our timeline is tight - aiming to complete intake and initial review by the end of the month.

Attendees on our side: Alex Turner (security lead), Priya Singh (compliance).

Thanks,
Alex Turner

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@vitalscope.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood follow-up + security questionnaires

Alex - great to meet you earlier, thanks for the note. Looping in Marissa (Legal) and Jordan (SE) so we can cover procurement/engineering items you may surface.

Attached is our preliminary SIG spreadsheet (SIG-Redwood-vitalscope-20270411.xlsx) and a short CAIQ export. A few clarifying questions from our side to speed the review:

1) Scope: Do you expect Redwood to process PHI on behalf of VitalScope (i.e., will VitalScope send any protected health information into the service)?
2) Data residency: Are you constrained to a specific region or cloud region for processing/storage (e.g., US-only, EU)?
3) Audit preference: Do you need a copy of our SOC 2 Type II report or is an attest letter + SOC 2 coverage matrix sufficient for initial review?
4) Escrow / Subprocessor: Any preferred contract language or strict disallowed subprocessors we should be aware of?

If helpful, Jordan can join a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk through technical controls and our deployment options (hosted vs. dedicated/private) that affect isolation and data residency.

Next steps suggested: 1) You confirm answers to the four clarifying Qs above, 2) we provide the CAIQ + SOC2 pointer, 3) schedule a SE call if needed.

Thanks - attaching the SIG file now.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: SIG-Redwood-vitalscope-20270411.xlsx (stub)]

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@vitalscope.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@vitalscope.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood follow-up + security questionnaires

Thanks Camila - answers inline below. I'm copying Priya from compliance so she has context.

1) PHI: Yes - some workloads will include PHI (e.g., de-identified patient notes initially, but future scope may include limited PHI identifiers). We will need confirmation that Redwood supports HIPAA and is willing to sign a BAA.

2) Data residency: US-only processing is preferred for the first phase. We may consider EU later.

3) Audit preference: We prefer to see the SOC 2 Type II report if possible. If there are gating issues to share the full report, an attest letter plus a coverage matrix is acceptable for the intake. Please let us know which you can provide.

4) Subprocessors: No strict disallowed subprocessors, but we do require disclosure of any subprocessors that store or process PHI.

A couple of extra technical items for Jordan:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood retains input text in persistent logs by default, and if so, whether that can be disabled for a dedicated deployment?
- Does Redwood offer encryption for KV caches at rest, and what KMS integrations are supported?

I've attached our completed vendor-intake form for reference.

Best,
Alex Turner
Head of InfoSec
VitalScope

[Attachment: vendor-intake-form-vitalscope-completed.pdf (stub)]

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@vitalscope.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-13T14:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood follow-up + security questionnaires

Alex - thanks for the quick responses and the completed intake. A few notes / answers below and next steps: 

• SOC 2: We can provide either the SOC 2 Type II report under an NDA or an attest letter + coverage matrix for initial review. Our most recent Type II period ended 2026-12-31; we expect the next attestation update in Q3 2027. If you want the report, I'll route it via our secure file share (or we can execute an NDA first).

• HIPAA / BAA: Redwood supports HIPAA-covered workloads under our Private and Dedicated offerings. We are willing to sign a BAA for covered uses - Marissa (Legal) can lead that conversation.

• PHI & logs: For Dedicated and Private deployments, persistent logging of input text can be disabled; hosted customers can opt into reduced retention and per-customer controls. Jordan can follow up with the exact config flags.

• KV cache & KMS: KV cache at rest can be encrypted; we support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS and GCP KMS in Private/Dedicated. 

Attachments included: a normalized CAIQ export and the updated SIG response. See files: CAIQ-Redwood-response-20270413.pdf and SIG-Redwood-vitalscope-20270411.xlsx.

Next steps: 
1) Marissa will follow up on the BAA language and NDA pathway (she'll reach out separately).
2) If helpful, Jordan - can you join a 30-minute technical sync tomorrow at 10am PT? Alex/Priya, does that time work?
3) I'll upload the SOC 2 Type II report via secure link if you confirm NDA/recipient list.

Thanks - happy to move quickly to keep you on your timeline.

Best regards,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
